Podilsk New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Podilsk, Ukraine

Demolished. Per a 1994 Jewish Preservation Committee expedition, this cemetery was established around 1910 (though the ESJF's own 2018 survey found the oldest surviving tombstone dated only to 1930); it appears on Russian topographic maps from 1914 and 1916-1917 and remains operational today. Podilsk (known as Birzula before 1935, then Kotovsk from 1935-2016) saw early 19th-century Jewish settlement, growing slowly to 95 residents (10%) by 1897; an 1882-1903 settlement ban preceded rapid early 20th-century growth as the town became an economic and transport hub, reaching 2,205 Jews by 1923 and 2,507 (25%) by 1926. Pogroms struck in 1905 and 1919; Rabbis Mordechai Shrabmachen and later Yosef Diment led the community. Population reached 2,375 by 1939. About 50 Jews were executed by Nazis in November 1941, with most of the community deported to Dubossary and shot; a 1942 railroad labor camp held Bukovina and Transylvania Jews. Some Jews returned postwar, with a small community and synagogue operating by 1946.
